title: Understand. Check. Explain.
narration: PolicyLens connects a public Kubernetes policy to a clear explanation and a reproducible configuration check. This walkthrough uses real results from the running Go API, presented as designed visuals rather than an app screen recording.

title: Every rule has a source.
narration: The collection contains six unmodified Kyverno policies. It covers privileged containers, non-root execution, privilege escalation, image tags, registries and application labels. Each definition is pinned to a Git revision, with its original source link and file digest.

title: One Pod. Six violations.
narration: Start with the failing payment API Pod. It requests privileged access, allows root execution and privilege escalation, uses the latest image tag from an unapproved registry, and has no application label. Kyverno evaluates the manifest and returns six failures. A language model does not decide this result.

title: Correct the configuration.
narration: The corrected example disables privileged access and privilege escalation, requires non-root execution, uses an explicit image version from the example approved registry, and adds the application label. Running the same six policies again produces six passes, with no skipped rules or engine errors.

title: A small change. A precise failure.
narration: Now remove only the application label from the corrected Pod. Five policies still pass, and the label policy fails. This gives a concrete before-and-after example of regression diagnosis. These are recorded results from actual engine execution, not predicted outcomes.

title: Keep the evidence visible.
narration: Ask which image registries are allowed. PolicyLens retrieves supporting passages and links back to the pinned policy. The two registry names shown here are upstream examples. This demo uses source excerpts, not generated answers. Optional local language model generation is a separate integration.

title: No evidence? Say so.
narration: Ask how much annual leave you get. That question is outside this Kubernetes collection, so PolicyLens abstains instead of inventing an answer. The authored retrieval evaluation covers eighteen policy questions and six unrelated questions. That small test set does not establish general accuracy.

title: A backend you can explain.
narration: The React and TypeScript interface calls a Go REST service. A Go SDK and command line client use the same API. Kyverno runs with bounded inputs, concurrency and deadlines. Tests cover the API and real engine fixtures, while request IDs, readiness checks and metrics support troubleshooting.

title: Reproducible checks. Honest answers.
narration: The complete application can be shared through a free Cloudflare tunnel while its host stays online. Validation covers this six-rule pack offline; it does not certify a cluster or enforce admission. PolicyLens demonstrates backend engineering, evidence retrieval and clear boundaries, with room to grow into a broader generative AI platform.
